title: KICD GRADE 5 AGRICULTURE AND NUTRITION CURRICULUM DESIGN

specific_learning_outcomes: Identify signs of soil erosion in the school and local agricultural environment.
Demonstrate methods of soil recovery from eroded sites using organic mulch and contours.
Appreciate the importance of conserving soil for household and community food security.
suggested_learning_experiences: Learners walk around the school compound to observe and record rill and splash erosion signs.
Learners collect grass, dry leaves, and twigs to construct organic mulch over seedbeds.
Learners work collaboratively in small groups to construct miniature diversion channels and cover crops.
key_inquiry_questions: How does bare soil get eroded by rainwater?
How do dry leaves and organic mulch help retain soil moisture and fertility?
core_competencies: Critical thinking and problem solving (analyzing erosion patterns)
values: Responsibility (caring for school soil and vegetation)

assessment_rubric.exceeding: Accurately identifies subtle erosion indicators, constructs flawless organic mulching, and innovatively mentors peers.
assessment_rubric.meeting: Correctly identifies soil erosion signs and constructs effective organic mulch following instructions.
assessment_rubric.approaching: Identifies common erosion signs with guidance and partially constructs mulch with supervision.
assessment_rubric.below: Struggles to identify erosion signs and requires continuous direct intervention to place mulch.

specific_learning_outcomes: Explain simple rooftop rainwater harvesting techniques suitable for school and home gardens.
Construct simple water storage containers using cleaned recycled local plastic bottles and drums.
Advocate for prudent water conservation in agricultural production.
suggested_learning_experiences: Learners inspect roof gutters and downspouts to observe roof catchment dynamics.
Learners create simple drip irrigation prototypes using punctured 2-litre plastic bottles placed beside plant roots.
Learners discuss water rationing schedules for the school kitchen garden.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is rainwater harvesting critical during dry seasons in Kenya?
How can recycled plastic bottles be converted into efficient drip watering tools?

assessment_rubric.exceeding: Independently designs and tests innovative bottle drip irrigation systems with calibrated flow.
assessment_rubric.meeting: Constructs functional bottle drip irrigation systems and harvests rainwater proficiently.
assessment_rubric.approaching: Assembles bottle drip system with occasional teacher assistance.
assessment_rubric.below: Requires step-by-step assistance to puncture and position water containers.

specific_learning_outcomes: Differentiate indigenous African leafy vegetables (e.g. Managu, Terere, Kunde) from exotic varieties.
Prepare nursery seedbeds using fine tilth soil and compost manure.
Transplant healthy seedlings with proper root ball protection and initial watering.
suggested_learning_experiences: Learners visit local markets or gardens to sample indigenous vegetable leaves and seeds.
Learners prepare nursery beds, measure spacing, and incorporate well-rotted farmyard manure.
Learners transplant seedlings in late afternoon and apply shaded protective leafy covers.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are indigenous African leafy vegetables highly nutritious and drought tolerant?
Why should vegetable transplanting be done in the late afternoon?

assessment_rubric.exceeding: Masterfully prepares nursery beds, achieves 100% transplant survival rate, and educates peers on indigenous nutrition.
assessment_rubric.meeting: Prepares nursery beds with fine tilth and transplants seedlings adhering to spacing standards.
assessment_rubric.approaching: Prepares nursery beds with guidance; needs assistance in seedling root handling.
assessment_rubric.below: Damages seedling roots during transplanting and requires continuous supervision.

specific_learning_outcomes: Identify common poultry breeds suitable for backyard rearing in Kenya.
Demonstrate routine feeding and watering practices using local crop residue and clean drinkers.
Recognize common signs of ill health and distress in domestic birds.
suggested_learning_experiences: Learners observe local chicken breeds (Kienyeji, improved indigenous) in the community.
Learners formulate supplementary poultry feeds mixing crushed maize, greens, and clean oyster shells.
Learners clean and disinfect poultry feeding troughs using warm water and ash solution.
key_inquiry_questions: How does proper poultry shelter protect birds from predators and weather extremes?
Why is clean water essential for daily egg production and poultry vigor?

assessment_rubric.exceeding: Exemplarily demonstrates feed preparation, identifies early disease symptoms, and leads bird hygiene tasks.
assessment_rubric.meeting: Prepares standard poultry feed mixtures and cleans equipment effectively.
assessment_rubric.approaching: Assists in feed preparation; needs guidance on feeder disinfection.
assessment_rubric.below: Requires direct supervision to handle feed and identify sick birds.
